In 1910, a Norfolk lawyer named Arthur Morris kept seeing the same thing: a steadily employed worker needed a small loan, the banks turned him away for lack of collateral, and he was left with nowhere reputable to borrow. Morris decided a banking system that shut out most of the people it was meant to serve had a "weak spot" worth fixing, so he built a lender that lent on character and steady income, backed by two references and repaid in small installments. What made it matter wasn't any single loan, but that Morris turned the idea into a repeatable system and scaled it to more than a hundred Morris Plan banks across thirty-seven states. 
 A century later, the hard part is unchanged: making one good loan is easy; building a business that makes millions of them well is hard. Mercury is building a banking*-grade lending business, where credit extends the trust businesses already place in us to hold and move their money. We need a leader to turn that foundation into a thriving, responsibly-scaled business. 
 We’re looking for a Head of Product to own Mercury's lending business end-to-end: defining product strategy, leading a team of product managers and lending specialists, driving growth, and ultimately owning business performance and P&L outcomes. You will work closely with credit, sales and finance to grow originations while maintaining healthy approval rates, repayment performance, and loss outcomes.  
  *Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.  
 Key responsibilities 
 
  Own the business lending P&L and strategy:  Set the multi-year strategy - which products to build, which segments to serve, how to grow originations against economic and credit targets. Own the numbers. 
  Build and scale the lending org:    Recruit, develop, and lead a high-performing PM team,strong product build discipline, develop future leaders, and establish the operating cadence and culture that allow a lending business to move quickly without sacrificing rigor. 
  Take products from 0-1 to scale:   Launch and grow Mercury's lending products - term loans, lines of credit, and what comes next, and build the experimentation loop that compounds growth post-launch. 
  Partner with credit, underwriting, and risk  on credit policy, underwriting models, and eligibility.  
  Manage capital and lending partners:  Work with finance, capital markets, and banking/lending partners to keep the business well-capitalized and structured to scale, and own those relationships. 
  Balance growth with rigor:  Build a lending business that customers love while meeting the credit, risk, and compliance standards a regulated product demands— making the hard tradeoffs between speed, experience, and controls. 
  Align the lending ecosystem:  Bring together product, engineering, underwriting, risk, credit operations, data, compliance, legal, marketing, sales, support, and external partners to execute a cohesive lending strategy and deliver strong business outcomes. 
 
  Some things that might make you successful in a role like this:  
 
 We're looking for a leader who has built and scaled a business lending organization, with great product chops, the commercial instinct to grow it and the credit discipline to grow it responsibly, equally credible on portfolio economics with finance, credit policy with underwriting, and product strategy with engineering.

Open call for Founders / Founding Teams (Product Management / Engineering roles)   
 In 1973 at Xerox PARC, Bob Metcalfe sketched a way for many computers to share a single wire — borrowing the throughput math from his study of Hawaii's ALOHAnet — and he and David Boggs built it and measured it until it held. Behind Ethernet was a two-person team that turned a contested idea into the measured standard now carrying almost all the world's wired traffic.  At Mercury, we’re looking to accelerate several of our AI products that our customers love like Command, CLI, and MCP.  We’re building for ambitious people of all kinds, and are a company made of founders and small technical teams trying to change the world - as part of that, we’re taking open applications for founders or small technical teams (Eng+) that want to work together on building the AI products of the future.  This isn't a fixed role. We expect the nature of work is changing, and small teams of people paired with AI product surface and autonomy to build can create 10x outcomes. Apply as a small team or as an individual   Here are some things you’ll do on the job: 
 
 Find the problem. Work close enough to customers that you spot what matters before anyone assigns it to you — then decide it's worth building. 
 Build and automate the workflow end to end using Command, CLI, MCP, and the rest of our AI stack. 
 Ship to customers fast — quick understanding, tight iteration, deploy. 
 Measure the impact honestly, then do the next one. Kill what didn't move; double down on what did. 
 Run as an autonomous team — pick the target, ship the thing, own the outcome. 
 
 You should: 
 
 Have shipped something real -  a product, a tool, a company, or an open-source project people actually use. 
 Be dangerous across the stack: PMs who can prototype, engineers with product taste.  
 Have strong opinions about AI products and the judgment to recognize fast when one of them is wrong. 
 Hands experience building AI products with AI, and knowledge about RAG, evals, agent harnesses a plus 
 Move fast and measure. Expect most experiments to fail and treat that as the price of finding the ones that don't. 
 Care about craft where it's impactful and resist polishing what isn't. 
 Communicate clearly and own outcomes - we want real business impact, customer time/pain saved, and a path to scaling what works 
 
  Learn more about what we're building:  
 
  Mercury Command  — Complete financial work end-to-end with AI. Tell Mercury what to do in natural language; it stages the action and executes with your approval. 
  Mercury MCP & CLI  — Give your AI agents direct access to verified financial data, or work with your Mercury account straight from the terminal. 
  The bank of the future knows your business  — Immad on what we're building toward and why now is the moment.

 Submit your application and our recruiting team will follow up. We're genuinely open to connecting with founders and teams at any stage — whether you're a strong fit for something we're actively building toward right now, or this is the start of a longer relationship we pick back up when the opportunity is right. If you're building, we want to know you.

 — Ada Lovelace, 1843 
 What Lovelace saw in the loom was the pattern — flowers and leaves, repeated faithfully, each one begun by a hand that chose it. Mercury is built from patterns too. Every component, every interaction our customers come to trust, starts with someone deciding how it should go, and making it good enough to be used again and again. Tending those patterns, and giving everyone at Mercury the means to weave with them, is the work of our Design System team, and the north star of this role. 
 As a Senior Frontend Engineer on the Design Systems team, you will build and care for those patterns: the components and foundations that everything else at Mercury is built on. Done well, a single decision here makes every product team faster. 
 The ground under that work is shifting, though. Software is being built in new ways, and AI is increasingly part of how design systems are made and used. We are looking for someone who is fluent at that intersection: deeply versed in design systems, and equally as serious about what it takes to build a system that holds up at the leading edge of AI.

 Build and maintain the components, patterns, and foundations (tokens, type, color, layout) that Mercury's product is woven from, holding a high bar for accessibility, performance, and pixel-level craft.

 Lead projects that ship new UI patterns to solve real pain points for product teams, helping them build better experiences faster. 
 Develop a design system that's as ready for AI as it is for people, applying the technology to create leveraged outcomes. 
 Invest in the design system's prototyping experience, shaping the next iteration of how our design function rapidly prototypes, iterates on the product, and explores new concepts. 
 Raise the craft and AI fluency of the people around you, through mentorship and clear best practices. 
 
  The ideal candidate for the role:  
 We're looking for someone who cares about the foundational work that lets other people do their best work, and who's eager to help define what a design system means in a world where agents build alongside us. A successful candidate will likely have: 
 
 4+ years of frontend development, with deep experience in React, TypeScript, and modern web technologies. 
 Experience building or maintaining a design system or shared component library. 
 A thorough command of modern frontend tooling: build systems, CI/CD, and testing. 
 High agency, and comfort creating clarity in ambiguous spaces. You take ownership and move without waiting for a defined path. 
 First-principles systems thinking that stays oriented to outcomes. You make clear decisions that drive toward results instead of getting stuck in open questions. 
 Strong product taste, and an instinct for leverage: the change that makes many teams better, not the one component polished in isolation. 
 Hands-on fluency at the intersection of AI and software development: a real command of how emerging AI paradigms are changing the way software gets built, and the ability to turn that into practical leverage, both for the design system itself and for the people who build on it.

In 1954, architect Eero Saarinen designed a radically modern bank branch for Irwin Union in Columbus, Indiana. With glass walls, no private offices, and a floor plan that invited openness, it embodied a new kind of transparency in finance. The building was surrounded by trees, furnished by Herman Miller, and featured rustic brick flooring. Today, that space is a conference center, and that spirit of design-forward thinking in banking* feels all but extinct.  Mercury believes that level of care and craft in design has been lost in modern finance, and we’re building products that bring it back. Cards and credit are built on complicated systems and inherited conventions, but our customers shouldn’t have to experience that complexity. We believe thoughtful design can turn something traditionally transactional into an experience that feels simple, intuitive, and distinctly Mercury.  We’re looking for a Senior Product Designer to join our Cards & Credit team. You’ll tackle complex product problems, question inherited assumptions, and shape experiences that help startups spend less time banking and more time building.  In this role, you’ll: 
 
 Own meaningful Cards & Credit product problems from initial framing through shipped experience, partnering closely with Product and Engineering to understand the problem and shape what we should build. 
 Turn complicated systems, requirements, and edge cases into experiences that feel remarkably simple and intuitive. 
 Work across the entire design stack, from framing problems and exploring concepts to workflows, detailed interactions, visual design, prototyping, and final implementation.

 Collaborate with Mercury’s Brand team on physical cards and related products, creating a cohesive experience between the objects our customers hold and the product experiences surrounding them. 
 Develop a deep understanding of our customers, communicate the reasoning behind your decisions clearly, and work through tradeoffs with your partners to arrive at the strongest solution. 
 
 What you’ll bring: 
 
 A strong portfolio of product work demonstrating exceptional product thinking, interaction design, and visual craft. 
 An ability to understand complicated systems and turn them into simple, thoughtful product experiences. 
 Deep curiosity about why a problem exists before deciding how to solve it, with a willingness to question assumptions and work from first principles. 
 Real ambition for the work itself. You want to do the best work of your career here, and you’re energized by being surrounded by people who hold themselves to the same bar. 
 A high bar for craft and the judgment to know where additional thought and detail meaningfully improve an experience. 
 Comfort navigating ambiguity and taking ownership without waiting for every requirement to be defined. 
 A habit of exploring multiple possibilities, prototyping ideas, and changing direction when a stronger solution emerges. 
 Strong communication and collaboration skills, including the ability to articulate your thinking, explain tradeoffs, and build conviction with Product and Engineering partners.

 You don’t need a background in banking, fintech, cards, or credit. We care much more about whether you’ve demonstrated the ability to understand complicated problems and turn them into simple, thoughtful product experiences.

"Start where you are. Use what you have. Do what you can." – Arthur Ashe   
 There's a version of investment products legal work that's mostly about maintaining what already exists. Reviewing disclosures that haven't changed in years, advising on products whose architecture was set long before you arrived. This isn't that. Mercury Treasury and Mercury Invest* are in some ways still taking shape and must continually rise to the occasion to meet evolving customer needs. The regulatory frameworks are complex, the product roadmap is ambitious, and the person in this role will have a direct hand in the high quality customer experience we deliver to Mercury users. 
  Who we are:  
 Since 2019, Mercury has been on a mission to reinvent banking** for the modern age. We blend elegant design and cutting-edge technology to offer checking and savings accounts, debit cards, payment services, credit products, cash management tools, and sophisticated analytics. Everything we build reflects our belief that finance should be thoughtfully crafted, fast, transparent, and frictionless. 
  About the team:  
 Our Product & Regulatory Legal team operates like the rest of Mercury: with urgency, curiosity, and a bias toward action. We embed with product teams from early ideation through launch, working alongside engineers, designers, and compliance partners to get products right. We move fast, we take ownership, and we don't wait to be asked: If something needs figuring out, we’re up to the task. 
  What you'll do:  
 
  Own the investment products portfolio:  Serve as the primary legal advisor for Mercury Treasury and Mercury Invest, the products through which Mercury's business and consumer customers access non-deposit investment products. You'll advise across the full product life cycle, including everything from supporting new feature development, drafting disclosures, calibrating on content for marketing and customer communications, and advising on operational matters with regulatory impacts. 
  Work across the company:  This role sits at the intersection of product, compliance, risk, engineering, and operations. You'll build relationships across all of these functions and bring legal perspective into conversations early; not as a checkpoint, but as a low ego, high ownership thought partner. 
  Advise and support compliance:  You'll work closely with Mercury's compliance team on regulatory matters affecting investment products, interpreting requirements, pressure-testing approaches, and supporting examination readiness with FINRA and the SEC. 
  Flex and grow:  While investment products are your home base, you'll also have opportunities to contribute across Legal on other product areas, gaining new experiences and broadening your expertise over time. 
  Use AI intentionally:  Bring a working knowledge of AI tools in legal workflows and a genuine interest in finding new ways to drive efficiency. We're building a legal team that works smarter, not just harder. 
  Be a storyteller:  Translate dense regulatory concepts into straightforward, energizing narratives for product teams and other stakeholders as well as external audiences. 
  Stay curious and agile:  Embrace each new regulation, market shift, or product pivot as a learning opportunity. Mercury's regulatory landscape is evolving quickly, and the scope of this role will grow with it. This is not a maintenance-only role. 
 
  What you should have:  
 
 6+ years of legal experience, with at least 2 of those years focused on non-deposit investment products. 
 Familiarity with the Investment Advisers Act, Securities Act, Investment Company Act, Regulation Best Interest, Form CRS/ADV, FINRA rules, and related regulatory frameworks. 
 Some in-house experience is preferred but not required. Bonus points for exposure to regulatory agencies relevant to these products, whether as a member of agency staff or as part of an industry role. 
 Exceptional communication skills. You know your audience and you tailor accordingly. You're as precise in a Slack thread as you are in a regulatory filing, and you know the value of a well-selected emoji in one versus the other. 
 A proactive sense of ownership. You're never afraid to say "I don't know, but I'll find out." 
 Strong working knowledge of AI use cases within legal roles and/or financial services generally and genuine interest in using AI to drive efficiency in your work. 
 Some additional experience outside the investments/brokerage space. The right candidate brings a broader foundation in financial services, payments, or fintech. 
 
  What will make you successful here:  
 Mercury is a place where legal counsel are expected to have a point of view. Not just about what the regulation requires, but about how the product can meet that bar in a way that's elegant, scalable, and good for customers. The people who thrive on this team treat ambiguity as an invitation rather than a reason to pause. They read a regulation and think about what it  permits , not just what it prohibits.  
 You'll also spend a meaningful amount of your time on work that doesn't look like traditional legal practice: scoping cross-functional projects, pressure-testing product designs, building operational processes alongside compliance and ops partners. If you're someone who gets energy from that kind of work, and who measures their own impact by whether the product got better and not just whether the memo was airtight, you'll do well here.

 Mercury is on a mission to defy those expectations. We're a financial technology company that helps startups spend less time banking* and more time building. We believe that the key to our success revolves around thoughtful design — and we hold the craft of that design to an exceptionally high standard. We're looking for a Staff Brand Designer who sets that bar: someone whose eye is so precise, and whose execution is so considered, that the work around them gets better just by virtue of their presence. 
 This is a role for a designer who sweats the details that most people don't notice — the type hierarchy, the negative space, the grid, the crop.  Mixpanel is the leading product intelligence and analytics platform, trusted by more than 29,000 companies to help understand how people use the products they build.  At Mixpanel, we believe design excellence is a competitive moat. In a world where AI makes it easier than ever to ship, we believe the quality of the experience — how it feels, how it builds trust, how it handles complexity with grace — that separates good products from great ones. 
 As a Staff Design Engineer at Mixpanel, you'll sit within the design organization and lead the transformation of our design system from a component library into something far more important:  the infrastructure that powers how we design, build, and ship in an AI-native world.  You'll encode our craft, standards, and vision directly into the systems, tools, and workflows that every designer, engineer, and AI agent in our org builds on. 
 This isn't a maintenance or systems stewardship role. It's a transformative one. You'll work at the frontier of what design and engineering collaboration looks like when AI writes most of the code, agents prototype from intent, and the design system is less a library and more a living foundation for everything we ship. 
 You'll be the designer who ships production code. The engineer who holds an uncompromising craft bar. The person who sees the future of how Mixpanel will look and behave in an AI-native world, and builds the infrastructure to make it real. 
 What you'll do 
 Build the infrastructure for an AI-native design practice 
 Translate Mixpanel's design standards, principles, and taste into systems that live in the code. Build a token system, component library, documentation, and guidelines that AI agents, AI coding tools, and AI prototyping workflows can reliably build on. Evolve our design system to be foundational infrastructure for AI-assisted workflows. 
 Shape how Mixpanel looks and behaves in an AI-native world 
 Sit within the product design team and collaborate on reimagining Mixpanel for a world where interfaces are conversational, agentic, and adaptive.  Own the bridge between design and code 
 Build systems that connect design to code and keep the two in sync. Define what "shippable" looks like as AI writes more of the code. Work directly in the codebase. Ship PRs that improve the product. Make design a force multiplier for engineering, not a bottleneck. 
 Stand up prototyping and AI tooling infrastructure 
 Build the workflows, tools, and infrastructure that let designers and PMs prototype at high fidelity, with working code, real components, and interactive states, without waiting on engineering. Identify the places where design and engineering lose time, intent, or quality in the handoff, and build AI-powered workflows that close those gaps. 
 Set and model the craft bar 
 Establish what great looks like — not through documentation alone, but through the quality of what you ship. Enable designers to work more code-adjacent and engineers to build with better components. Stay ahead of how AI is changing EPD workflows and bring that change into the org responsibly.

 The design system is a reliable foundation that AI tools and agents build on, not an obstacle they work around

Why You'll Love This Role:    
  We are seeking a Learning Experience Designer (LXD), Core to serve as a grade-level lead in the design and production of high-quality instructional materials for Newsela’s core secondary ELA curriculum. This role is ideal for a hands-on curriculum builder with strong ELA content and pedagogy expertise who is passionate about creating engaging, standards-aligned lessons, texts, and assessments—and who is energized by owning the quality and coherence of an entire grade level of instruction.  
  As a grade-level lead, you are accountable for the quality of everything that ships at your grade: the development of scopes and sequences for units; development and review of teacher- and student-facing materials; content from internal teams, external contributors, and AI-supported workflows; and making the day-to-day judgment calls that keep units aligned to standards, the curriculum model, and Newsela’s quality bar. You’ll collaborate with other content teams and leaders in developing, refining, and implementing program-level frameworks and quality guidelines, and you'll own their consistent application at your grade.  
  If you love the craft of curriculum—shaping it, improving it, and helping others make it better—this role is an opportunity to put your fingerprints on every lesson students at your grade level experience.  
   What You'll Be Doing:   
   Grade-Level Ownership   
 
   Grade-Level Leadership:  Serve as the grade-level lead and subject-matter point of contact for your assigned grade, owning the resolution of content and alignment issues across workstreams and being the person internal teams and external contributors count on for timely, well-reasoned answers.  
   Coherence & Consistency:  Take accountability for ensuring that lessons, texts, and assessments at your grade level form a coherent arc—consistent in structure, voice, rigor, and fidelity to the curriculum model from the first unit to the last.  
   Standards Alignment:  Hold final grade-level responsibility for verifying that all materials align to the relevant state ELA standards and frameworks, maintaining grade-level rigor while ensuring accessibility for diverse learners.  
 
   Curriculum Design & Content Creation   
 
   Scope & Sequence Development:  Support the development of grade-level scopes and sequences, ensuring the progression of texts, skills, and standards builds knowledge coherently across units and reflects established instructional frameworks.  
   Lesson Development:  Support the development of teacher-facing and student-facing lessons and other materials that model rigorous, scaffolded, standards-aligned instruction based on established instructional frameworks and product specifications, upholding the Newsela instructional framework.  
   Assessment Development:  Draft and refine formative and summative assessment items, rubrics, and performance tasks that accurately measure student mastery of grade-level standards and follow assessment best practices.  
   Scaffolding & Access:  Build embedded scaffolds and differentiation—graphic organizers, sentence frames, leveled vocabulary supports—so complex, high-interest content is accessible to all learners, including multilingual learners and striving readers, without diluting rigor.  
 
   Review & Quality Assurance at Scale   
 
   Human Review at Scale:  Own the review of contributor- and AI-generated lessons, activities, and assessments at your grade, providing focused editorial and pedagogical feedback grounded in Newsela guidelines to ensure accuracy, engagement, and fidelity to the curriculum model.  
   AI-Supported Production:  Support the iterative refinement of AI prompts and specifications that power stages of lesson design and production, helping translate instructional blueprints into consistent, high-quality content at scale.  
   Quality Documentation:  Collaborate in developing, refining, and implementing the rubrics, checklists, and conventions that guide contributors and AI tools, proposing improvements based on what you see at your grade level.  
 
   Collaboration & Workflow   
 
   Cross-Team Partnership:  Collaborate closely with senior designers, lesson and assessment writers, ELD specialists, and product and technology teams to integrate feedback, align across grade levels, and support content digitization and platform experience.  
   Organization & Delivery:  Prioritize and re-prioritize in line with business needs, delivering work on time and to Newsela’s standards of quality, and communicating progress and blockers proactively.  
 
   About You:   
 
   Education:  Bachelor’s degree in English, Education, Curriculum & Instruction, or a related field.  
   Experience:  5+ years of experience in secondary ELA curriculum development, instructional design, or content creation, preferably for an educational technology or publishing company (school- or district-based curriculum development experience also considered). A high school emphasis is welcome given near-term needs.  
   ELA Expertise:  Strong working knowledge of secondary ELA pedagogy and state standards and frameworks such as CCSS, including reading development, writing instruction, and assessment best practices.  
   Content Skills:  Excellent English writing and editing, with a demonstrated ability to produce polished, standards-aligned instructional content and to give clear, useful feedback to other writers.  
   Judgment & Detail:  A judicious eye for quality and acute attention to detail when reviewing materials, with the ability to make sound, well-reasoned content decisions independently.  
   Accountability:  A strong ownership mindset—you take responsibility for outcomes at your grade level, follow through on commitments, surface risks early, and hold yourself and others to a high bar.  
   AI Fluency:  Comfort and fluency with AI tools, and an interest in using them to accelerate high-quality content development without sacrificing pedagogical rigor.  
   Ways of Working:  Strong organizational and verbal communication skills, with the ability to manage multiple workstreams and prioritize in conjunction with business needs.  
 
   Preferred   
 
  Prior classroom teaching experience in secondary ELA.  
  Experience contributing to a core (basal) ELA curriculum at a curriculum provider.  
  Experience creating resources or scaffolds for multilingual learners and striving readers.  
  Experience reviewing or guiding the work of contributors, freelancers, or vendor teams.  
  Experience with digital content authoring tools or content management systems (CMS).  
  Master’s degree in English, Education, Curriculum & Instruction, or a related field.  
 
   
   All offers of employment are contingent upon the successful completion of a background check as part of our pre-employment process.   
   
   Why you’ll love working at Newsela:   
 
   Health & Wellness:  Comprehensive medical benefits with employer contribution to premiums and to HSA accounts. Additional benefits such as gym reimbursement, pet insurance, free access to the Calm app, Rocket Lawyer and more to help you stay healthy: mind, body, and soul.   
   Work From Home:  We are a fully remote company. We provide a monthly tech stipend to support your WFH needs!  
   Supporting ALL Families:  Inclusive benefits to support you and your family, including parental leave, fertility support, adoption, and more!   
   Financial Wellbeing:  Invest in your future with our 401(k) plan, which includes a employer match to help you build long-term financial security.  
   Time Off:  Flexible PTO, paid sick time off, company holidays plus winter break (Dec 24th - Jan 1st).  
   Professional Development:    Newsela offers an annual learning and development allowance to employees to attend external training sessions, classes, workshops, conferences, and educational materials to foster professional growth within their current role and career aspirations at Newsela.  
   Make A Difference:  No matter your role or department, the work you do each day helps share the future of education and improves the lives of students and teachers.  
 
   About Newsela:   
  Newsela is a leading education technology company dedicated to meaningful classroom learning for every student. We deliver integrated, AI-powered solutions designed to unlock student engagement, empower teachers, and drive meaningful learning outcomes. Our suite of products supports knowledge and skill development, writing practice, daily instruction, assessment, and data-informed decision-making across K–12 classrooms. Grounded in learning science research, Newsela’s solutions integrate content, assessment, and analytics to help educators track progress, understand student outcomes, and deliver high-impact instruction that supports every learner.

c89033da3160a313.title: Product Designer, AI Experience
c89033da3160a313.jd:
Omada Health is on a mission to bend the curve of chronic disease. 
  Job overview:     
 We’re hiring for a seasoned Product Designer that will focus on our AI Experience, helping to define how intelligent, personalized experiences show up across Omada’s member and care ecosystem. This role sits at the intersection of product design, AI interaction design, service design, behavior change, and human-centered care.  
 This role focuses on the connective tissue between AI, product, behavior change, and human care. You will help define when AI should speak, when it should stay quiet, when it should guide, when it should recommend, and when it should escalate to a coach, clinician, or specialist.  
 We’re looking for a designer who can operate at the level of today’s most ambitious AI product teams: shaping new interaction models, prototyping quickly with AI tools, translating complex capabilities into intuitive experiences, and partnering deeply with product, engineering, data, research, clinical, and care teams to bring intelligent products to life responsibly.  
 This is not an ML engineering or AI research role. You will partner closely with AI, data science, engineering, clinical, care, research, content, and product teams to translate emerging AI capabilities into useful, trustworthy, clinically appropriate, and buildable member and care experiences.  
  Your Impact:   
 As a Product Designer you will...  
 
 Lead product and experience design for AI-supported member experiences across key moments in the health journey.  
 Define interaction models for intelligent guidance, recommendations, nudges, reflection, progress feedback, handoffs, and human-in-the-loop support.  
 Shape how AI and human care teams work together across digital and service touchpoints, ensuring the experience feels coherent, trustworthy, clinically appropriate, and easy to understand.  
 Translate concepts like motivation, trust, empathy, safety, personalization, consent, care continuity, and escalation into concrete design patterns teams can build, test, and scale.  
 Prototype early and often using modern design and AI tools, including conversational flows, simulated experiences, prompt-based prototypes, coded prototypes, service prototypes, and interactive concepts.  
 Partner with Product, AI, Data Science, Engineering, Clinical, Research, Content, Care Platform, and Design leadership to align user needs, business goals, technical capabilities, and care workflows.  
 Help define when intelligence should feel ambient versus explicit, how personalization is represented, and how recommendations or next-best actions are communicated.  
 Contribute to prompt, agent, voice, tone, and conversational experience patterns in partnership with AI, content, product, and engineering teams.  
 Help define evaluation loops for AI-powered experiences, including how teams assess clarity, trust, usefulness, safety, comprehension, follow-through, and member value.  
 Apply service blueprinting, journey mapping, and systems thinking to design across both member-facing and internal care team experiences.  
 Work with behavioral science, personalization, data science, machine learning, and care operations partners to translate complex inputs into practical experience patterns.  
 Create high-quality design artifacts, including journey maps, service blueprints, flows, wireframes, prototypes, interaction models, experience principles, and high-fidelity interface designs.  
 Influence senior stakeholders through clear storytelling, strong design rationale, and a deep understanding of member needs, business goals, technical constraints, and care delivery realities.  
 
  About you:   
 
 8+ years of experience in product design, UX design, experience design, service design, interaction design, or related fields.  
 A portfolio that demonstrates strong product thinking, interaction design, systems thinking, prototyping, and high-quality execution across complex digital products.  
 Experience designing AI-powered, personalized, data-informed, conversational, recommendation-based, or intelligent product experiences.  
 Experience designing across multiple surfaces, workflows, users, service touchpoints, or human handoff moments.  
 Strong product, interaction, and visual design craft, with the ability to make ambiguous ideas tangible through prototypes, flows, systems, and clear design artifacts.  
 Comfort using AI tools as part of your design workflow to explore ideas, prototype, synthesize research, generate concepts, evaluate directions, or build lightweight experiences.  
 Experience designing experiences that involve trust, safety, explainability, consent, escalation, sensitive interventions, clinical appropriateness, or human-in-the-loop support.  
 Experience shaping voice and tone systems, content patterns, branded assistants, intelligent guidance systems, or conversational product experiences.  
 Experience with service blueprinting, journey mapping, systems thinking, or designing across both member-facing and internal care team experiences.  
 Experience working with behavioral science, personalization, data science, machine learning, or care operations teams.  
 A thoughtful perspective on how intelligent products should communicate, behave, earn trust, and support users across different moments of care.  
 Excellent communication and storytelling skills, with the ability to influence senior stakeholders and align teams around a clear experience direction.  
 
  Bonus Points for:   
 
 Experience designing for healthcare, wellness, behavior change, chronic care, coaching, clinical workflows, specialist care, or longitudinal care delivery.  
 Experience working closely with AI research, ML engineering, data science, or applied AI teams.  
 Experience prototyping AI features, prompt-based experiences, agentic flows, or conversational product experiences.  
 Experience defining or contributing to AI evaluation loops, including how teams assess quality, trust, comprehension, usefulness, safety, or behavioral impact.  
 Experience using tools such as Figma Make, Cursor, Claude Code, Replit, v0, ChatGPT, Gemini, or similar tools to prototype, build, evaluate, or accelerate design exploration.  
 Experience working in ambiguous, fast-moving environments where new product patterns, technical capabilities, and user expectations are still emerging.  
 You are a strong product designer who can think in systems, not just screens.  
 You understand that AI experience design is not just about chat. It is about shaping how intelligence appears, behaves, supports, recommends, escalates, and builds trust across an ecosystem.  
 You are curious about AI and already use AI tools to think, prototype, build, or evaluate ideas.  
 You can translate complex capabilities into experiences that feel simple, useful, trustworthy, and clinically appropriate.  
 You can zoom out to define principles, systems, and service models, then zoom in to refine interaction details, flows, and product moments.  
 You know how to collaborate deeply with technical, clinical, operational, and product partners.  
 You care about craft, but you also know how to move quickly and learn through prototypes.  
 You bring a strong point of view, but you know how to build alignment across teams.  
 
  Our Design Roots   
 Omada was founded in 2011 out of IDEO, where our founders explored how human-centered design could be applied to chronic health challenges. What began as an internal project grounded in deep user research evolved into a new approach to digital care.  
 That origin continues to shape how we work today. We place a strong emphasis on understanding real human needs, designing from first principles, and creating experiences that are not only effective, but engaging and thoughtfully crafted.  
 Design is not a layer at Omada. It is foundational to how we build products, make decisions, and deliver care. As Omada evolves into a more intelligent, personalized, and daily care platform, this role will help define how AI works alongside coaches, clinicians, specialists, and members to make care feel more timely, adaptive, coordinated, emotionally resonant, clinically appropriate, and deeply human. 
  Benefits:  
 
 Competitive salary with generous annual cash bonus 
 Equity grants 
 Employee stock purchasing plan (ESPP) 
 Remote first work from home culture 
 Flexible Time Off to help you rest, recharge, and connect with loved ones 
 Generous parental leave 
 Health, dental, and vision insurance (and above market employer contributions) 
 401k retirement savings plan 
 Lifestyle Spending Account (LSA) 
 Mental Health Support Solutions 
 ...and more! 
 
 It takes a village to change health care. As we build together toward our mission, we strive to embody the following values in our day-to-day work. We hope these hold meaning for you as well as you consider Omada! 
 
  Cultivate Trust.  We listen closely and we operate with kindness. We provide respectful and candid feedback to each other. 
  Seek Context.  We ask to understand and we build connections. We do our research up front to move faster down the road. 
  Act Boldly.  We innovate daily to solve problems, improve processes, and find new opportunities for our members and customers. 
  Deliver Results.  We reward impact above output. We set a high bar, we’re not afraid to fail, and we take pride in our work. 
  Succeed Together.  We prioritize Omada’s progress above team or individual. We have fun as we get stuff done, and we celebrate together.  
  Remember Why We’re Here.  We push through the challenges of changing health care because we know the destination is worth it. 
 
  About Omada Health:  Omada Health (Nasdaq: OMDA) is reverse engineering the way healthcare is delivered in America, putting the space between doctor visits–where health is won or lost–at the center of care. Today's healthcare system poorly serves chronic conditions that require ongoing support outside of the exam room, like obesity, diabetes, hypertension, cholesterol, and musculoskeletal conditions. Omada’s virtual-first model combines human-led care teams, connected devices, and AI-enabled technology to deliver personalized care at scale, including support for GLP-1 therapy. Omada has served more than two million members since launch across 2,000+ employers, health plans, pharmacy benefit managers, and health systems. Learn more at omadahealth.com.

Natera is currently seeking a Bioinformatics Manager to join the Bioinformatics team focused on Oncology Product Development. In this role, the individual will manage a team of Bioinformaticians and Data Scientists and provide technical leadership in the design, development and validation of ctDNA-based diagnostic tests. This position requires extensive cross-functional collaboration with biostatistics, molecular biology, software engineering and commercial departments. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in bioinformatics and data science, optimally with experience in the analysis or modeling of DNA methylation data, and an established record of project and technical leadership.  
   PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES:   
 
  Lead the effort to develop, optimize, and improve tools and analysis pipelines for diagnostic tests, including the detection of cancer-associated variants or methylation patterns and the implementation of evidence-based quality control thresholds.  
  Provide technical leadership for product development projects by representing the team in cross-functional interactions and moving products through the full development process, from research through commercial launch.  
  Supervise bioinformatics scientists and data scientists, managing their technical contributions, prioritizing resources, and taking responsibility for their technical and professional development.  
  Provide input on experiment design, analysis and interpretation based on expert understanding of Natera’s technology and relevant mathematical principles.  
  Work at a high level of independence and responsibilities in carrying out assignments.  
  Contribute to our intellectual property portfolio.  
  Set standards for rigorous data analysis and lead the production of high-quality documentation.

  Master’s degree or Ph.D. in a quantitative discipline (bioinformatics, engineering, applied mathematics, statistics, or similar).  
  Minimum of 4-8 years of post-graduate experience in a data science and/or bioinformatics role and 1-3 years of experience as technical lead in diagnostics or a related field  
  Experience moving algorithm-based products through commercialization and launch in a medical or biological application such as diagnostic testing, medical imaging, or biotechnology  
 
   Desirable, but not required:   
 
  Prior experience analyzing or modeling DNA methylation data.

  Experience using Python or R for scientific data analysis and visualization.  
  Strong foundation in statistical modeling/machine learning, including probability theory and estimation/classification methods.  
  Experience with analysis of next-generation sequencing data, preferably including algorithm development or optimization.  
  Proven ability to apply mathematical principles to solve real estimation problems and implement practical solutions.  
  Excellent analytical, problem-solving and decision-making skills to independently make sound judgments and find creative solutions to moderately complex problems.  
  Experience leading technical projects, including defining and meeting project milestones, delegating tasks to more junior team members, and ensuring the quality of technical deliverables.

This is an exciting opportunity to lead a DevOps team at Natera, a global leader in precision medicine and genomics testing.  As a Senior Manager of the DevOps team inside our Data Science Production Engineering (DSPE) department, you will have the opportunity to work with Natera's diverse and ultra-large data sets (up to PB size), build upon the latest information and cloud technologies, create solutions for the most cutting-edge medical diagnostics and genomics applications, and make real impact by delivering reliable, efficient, high performance data/cloud/automation systems to support Natera's Lab Operations and Genetic Counselor/Lab Director teams, and ultimately impact patients' medical outcomes. 
  PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES:   
  Leadership  
 
 Lead a DevOps team, working closely with other DSPE teams, to develop, test, deploy, maintain, and update DSPE's data platforms, cloud platforms, automation systems, and analytics systems 
 Manage the DevOps team, to achieve the timely and efficient delivery of software products and systems with correct and robust functionality. 
 Train and coach team members on new technologies, procedures, and guidelines/best practices. 
 Create and maintain operational visibility (e.g., workload, productivity, etc.) of the DSPE DevOps team. 
 
  Technical  
 
 Translate DSPE's business needs and project requirements into technical specifications and implementation plans. 
 Working with DSPE leadership teams, create suitable system architecture and infrastructure design documents that can be efficiently implemented and maintained. 
 Maintain and optimize infrastructure performance, monitoring key system metrics including network I/O, disk I/O, memory allocation, and compute resource utilization. 
 Contribute to key development, testing, deployment, validation, maintenance, and update activities. 
 
  Quality, Compliance, and Documentation  
 
 Improve and enforce procedures for work efficiency, quality, and compliance. 
 Lead and manage the technical documentation's creation and maintenance/update for all DSPE DevOps owned software tools and systems, for example, design specifications, software verification and validation (V&V) protocols and reports, deployment/update/maintenance records, user guides, etc. 
 Create training materials, and contribute to training activities, on DSPE DevOps owned software tools and systems. 
 
  Cross-Functional  
 
 Engage proactively and directly with engineering and operational stakeholders to align infrastructure roadmaps, resolve technical dependencies, and report platform performance metrics. 
 Represent the DSPE DevOps team in stakeholder meetings. 
 
  QUALIFICATIONS:  
 
 Minimal Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Bioinformatics, or a related field.  Advanced degrees preferred. 
 Minimal 10 years of relevant industry experience for candidates with only a Bachelor's Degree.  Minimal 8 years of relevant industry experience for candidates with a Master's Degree.  Minimal 4 years of relevant industry experience for candidates with a Doctorate degree. 
 Minimal 3 years of working experience in a highly regulated environment, e.g., CLIA and/or FDA compliant settings. 
 Minimal 3 years of management experience leading a DevOps team, or a software development team. 
 Demonstrable experience in designing, delivering, and maintaining/updating custom-developed software tools or systems for production environments, preferable in high-throughput settings (e.g., heavy traffic and/or high computation load). 
 Demonstrable experience in creating software design specification documents, verification and validation documents, and user manuals. 
 
  KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES:  
 
 Excellent Python programming skills, with substantial cloud application and/or automation system development experience. 
 Proficient with RDBMS systems such as PostgreSQL and/or MySQL, and substantial working experience in for-production database-based application development. 
 Working knowledge in optimizing system architecture and individual components for performance, scalability, and/or reliability. 
 Proficiency in tool/system performance evaluation methods, and in-depth understanding of key factors, such as RAM, Disk IO, Network IO's impact on system/tool's performance. 
 Proficiency with AWS, and substantial working experience in developing for-production software tools/systems using AWS services. 
 Proficiency in SDLC and software development and testing methodologies. 
 Proficient Linux command line skills, and past Linux application development experience. 
 Past experience and working knowledge in genomics and bioinformatics technologies. 
 Good understanding and past working experience with genomics data, such as FASTQ, BAM, VCF files. 
 Proficiency in Git workflow and version control systems like GitHub and/or GitLab. 
 Past experience in developing automation solutions. 
 Preferred but not required: IaC skills and experiences, such as CloudFormation, Terraform, and/or Ansible. 
 Good documentation practices and coding style. 
 Strong verbal and written communication skills. 
 Strong interpersonal skills. 
 Strong integrity. 
 Team player. 
      
   Compensation & Total Rewards    
  This range reflects a good-faith estimate of the base pay we reasonably expect to offer at the time of  hire. Final compensation will vary based on experience, qualifications, and internal equity considerations.  
  This position is also eligible for additional compensation and benefits through Natera’s robust Total Rewards program, including:  
 
 
  Annual performance incentive bonus  
 
 
  Long-term equity awards  
 
 
  Comprehensive health benefits (medical, dental, vision)  
 
 
  401(k) with company match  
 
 
  Generous paid time off and company holidays  
 
 
  Additional wellness and work-life benefits  
 
 
    Compensation Range    $179,900  —  $224,850 USD       OUR OPPORTUNITY  
 Natera™ is a global leader in cell-free DNA (cfDNA) testing, dedicated to oncology, women’s health, and organ health. 949cc3e5acafe004.title: Staff Software Engineer in Test, Product Engineering
949cc3e5acafe004.jd:
Position Summary  
 Natera is at the forefront of personalized genetic testing, transforming the management of disease worldwide. As we scale our life-saving diagnostics, we are fundamentally transforming our approach to software quality and reliability. 
 We are seeking a highly technical, hands-on, and high-agency  Staff Software Engineer in Test  to join our Oncology Comprehensive Genomic Profiling (CGP) Product Engineering team. In this technical leadership role, you will serve as the test architect and lead developer for our product integration efforts, ensuring we deliver robust, on-time solutions across our CGP portfolio. You will act as the technical backbone for validating our most complex "Pillar" projects — operating across a sophisticated system of interconnected software products and distributed microservices. This demands deep, expert-level mastery of the system from two dimensions: working closely with architects to understand how it is built, and partnering with product managers to understand how it is used. You will translate that dual expertise into tests that reflect real-world complexity end-to-end — from order ingestion through lab execution to patient reporting — catching failure modes that only someone who truly knows the system would anticipate. You will bring an AI-native mindset as a core differentiator — leveraging advanced LLM methodologies to auto-generate test scenarios, analyze system logs, surface anomalies, and continuously optimize our CI/CD pipeline. 
 Crucially, while this is an individual contributor role, you will operate as a central leader — driving consensus, architectural alignment, and engineering excellence through influence rather than formal authority across Engineering, R&D, Commercial, and Clinical teams. You thrive in fluid environments, adapt quickly to change, and chart a clear path forward even amid unknowns. 
  Key Responsibilities  
  Technical Test Strategy & Integration Architecture  
 
  Define Integration Test Architecture : Architect and deploy comprehensive, automated system integration testing frameworks that mirror Natera's complex, multi-component service environments. 
  Contract-First Validation : Review and validate OpenAPI/Swagger REST specifications and Avro schemas for Kafka topics during the architecture phase to enforce strict communication protocols across microservices. 
  Shift Left Testing Initiative : Collaborate with Solution Architects early in the project lifecycle to isolate and address integration discrepancies within the design phase, long before a code freeze occurs. 
  AI-Native Framework Engineering : Pioneer the integration of LLMs and generative AI tools within the testing lifecycle to automate the synthesis of test logic from Level 2 (L2) specifications and behavior models (Gherkin syntax). 
 
  End-to-End Automation & Environment Governance  
 
  Long-Arc Workflow Automation : Author and execute high-fidelity integration test scenarios that traverse 3+ discrete systems across the order to report journey. 
  Resilient API & Event Testing : Minimize fragile UI automation by prioritizing asynchronous event verification (Kafka consumers/producers), webhook handlers, and database state checks. 
  Staging Guardrail Enforcement:  Support environment integrity by validating that intermediate component builds comply with version synchronization matrices (e.g., LIMS and PIPE dependency trees) prior to deployment. 
  AI-Driven Root Cause Analysis : Develop and embed log-scraping AI agents into the CI/CD pipeline to analyze multi-service exceptions, rapidly isolating fault vectors within complex distributed networks. 
 
  Technical Leadership & Cross-Functional Synergy  
 
  Cross-Functional Leadership via Influence : Lead and align cross-functional engineering pods, Solution Architects, and Digital Product Managers toward shared quality goals. You will drive architectural consensus and testing process adherence through technical credibility, persuasion, and partnership rather than formal reporting lines. 
  Technical Mentorship : Train and mentor Senior Software Quality Engineers (SQEs) and Software Engineers in Test across distributed scrum pods, championing systems thinking and advanced software automation practices. 
  Chaos Engineering & Resiliency Experiments : Introduce deliberate network latencies, container failures, and boundary conditions to rigorously validate the system's fail-soft and self-healing behaviors. 
 
  Qualifications  
 
  Professional Experience : 12+ years of active software development or test automation engineering experience, with at least 5 years in a senior or lead capacity, and a proven history of deploying automation structures for enterprise-grade distributed systems. 
  Technical Language Fluency : Expert programming capabilities in backend languages such as Java, Python, or Go, with hands-on experience in modern test automation frameworks including Playwright, and a solid grasp of containerized environments (Docker, Kubernetes). 
  Distributed Architecture Expertise : Hands-on technical mastery verifying microservices, REST/gRPC endpoints, and event-driven data hubs utilizing Apache Kafka or AWS SQS/SNS. 
  Cloud Native Proficiency:  Comprehensive experience utilizing AWS cloud native services (S3, Lambdas, CloudWatch) to track and mock backend infrastructure. 
  Regulated Domain Background : Prior exposure to highly structured, quality-critical engineering contexts (HealthTech, MedTech, or FinTech). Understanding of FDA design controls, IEC 62304, or HIPAA standards is highly advantageous. 
  Educational Background : Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a strictly quantitative discipline. 
 
  Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities  
 
  High Agency & Technical Initiative : You are a natural builder who thrives in fluid, fast-moving environments. Rather than waiting for predefined test specifications, you inspect code, audit requirements, chart a path forward amid unknowns, and implement frameworks proactively. 
  Deep Systems-Level Cognition : You bring expert-level mastery of the system from two dimensions — architectural depth and functional fluency. You can decipher how minor database modifications in upstream services impact report rendering down the line, catching failure modes that only someone who truly knows the system would anticipate. 
  Cross-Functional Leadership through Influence:  You operate as a central leader without formal authority — driving consensus, alignment, and engineering excellence across Engineering, R&D, Commercial, and Clinical teams through technical credibility, communication, and emotional intelligence. 
  User-Centric Validation Ethos : You understand that automated technical verifications are incomplete if the final end product degrades the clinical or laboratory operational experience.

4797c907bc5540e8.title: Senior Scientist, mRNA Design & Platform Innovation
4797c907bc5540e8.jd:
Company Overview:  
 Prime Medicine is a leading biotechnology company dedicated to creating and delivering the next generation of gene editing therapies to patients. The Company is leveraging its proprietary Prime Editing platform, a versatile, precise and efficient gene editing technology, to develop a new class of differentiated, one-time, potentially curative genetic therapies. Designed to make only the right edit at the right position within a gene while minimizing unwanted DNA modifications, Prime Editors have the potential to repair almost all types of genetic mutations and work in many different tissues, organs and cell types.   
 Prime Medicine is currently progressing a diversified portfolio of investigational therapeutic programs organized around our core areas of focus: hematology, immunology & oncology, liver and lung. Across each core area, Prime Medicine is focused initially on a set of high value programs, each targeting a disease with well-understood biology and a clearly defined clinical development and regulatory path, and each expected to provide the foundation for expansion into additional opportunities. For more information, please visit  www.primemedicine.com .   Prime Medicine was founded to bring the promise of gene editing to patients. We use Prime Editing, a next-generation “search-and-replace” technology that finds the precise place in the genome to edit and swaps in a corrected copy of DNA — designed to make only the right edit, in the right position, while minimizing unwanted changes elsewhere in the genome. A single Prime Editor can be tuned to correct the individual mutation found in a given patient, giving Prime Editing the potential to address the vast majority of known disease-causing genetic mutations, across many different tissues, organs, and cell types. 
  Position Overview  
 We are seeking an exceptionally driven, discovery-minded Senior Scientist to join our Platform Technology & Innovation team. This team sits at the very heart of Prime Medicine's innovation engine, reflecting our commitment to accelerating the next frontier of Prime Editing science. Its mission is to invent, establish, and rapidly implement the platform technologies that will define what new capabilities Prime Editing can achieve, and ultimately, what cures become possible for patients. 
 Reporting to the VP of Platform Technology & Innovation, the successful candidate will focus primarily on the design and engineering of RNA components for Prime Editing systems, while also applying molecular biology and Prime Editing expertise to other platform-level research challenges. Unlike most industry roles, this position offers a rare combination of deep, inventive science and direct translational impact with purposeful innovation where discoveries made here move rapidly and deliberately into programs working toward patient benefit. As the portfolio grows, this role is expected to take on additional scope. 
 This is a hands-on experimental role with a strong cross-functional dimension. The ideal candidate will bring deep expertise in RNA biology and mRNA engineering, a rigorous and creative scientific mindset, and an unwavering commitment to translating breakthrough science into real-world impact. The team is currently focused on extrahepatic delivery to the lung, laying the foundation for expansion into additional tissues and organs. 
  Primary Responsibilities  
 
 Design, construct, and systematically optimize novel mRNA architectures for Prime Editing applications, including UTR sequences, open reading frame design, codon usage, cap structures, poly(A) tail configurations, and RNA secondary structure, individually and in combination, to maximize expression, stability, translational efficiency, and in vivo performance 
 Design and execute well-controlled experiments to probe structure-function relationships in Prime Editing system components; generate clean, interpretable data that drives platform design decisions 
 Lead discovery efforts for novel therapeutic approaches and platform-level applications enabled by Prime Editing, beyond core mRNA design, partnering with program and platform teams to advance the most promising directions 
 Partner with cross-functional teams (Computational Biology, Technical Development, and program teams) as well as external collaborators and CROs to translate platform advances into program-specific solutions, including supporting Development Candidate nominations 
 Maintain active engagement with the scientific literature and emerging technologies in mRNA engineering, RNA biology, and gene editing to anticipate the next wave of innovation and identify external advances or collaborations worth pursuing 
 Communicate research findings clearly to internal scientific audiences; contribute to publications, patent filings, and conference presentations that advance Prime Medicine's scientific profile 
 Adhere to all laboratory safety requirements and procedures; author, review, and maintain accurate laboratory notebooks 
 Mentor and provide day-to-day scientific direction to research associates and interns/co-op students, with potential dotted-line oversight of additional staff as the team scales; contribute to a culture of scientific excellence, intellectual curiosity, and collaborative problem-solving 
 
   
  Preferred Qualifications  
 
 Ph.D. in Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, RNA Biology, Chemical Biology, or a closely related field, plus 5+ years of relevant postdoctoral and/or drug discovery research experience 
 Deep hands-on expertise in mRNA biology and engineering, including practical experience with in vitro transcription (IVT), UTR design and optimization, codon usage, RNA secondary structure, and the relationship between mRNA sequence design and protein expression outcomes 
 Experience working in a collaborative, cross-functional research environment with the ability to contribute meaningfully to team science while driving individual workstreams autonomously 
 Experience with next-generation or engineered RNA formats (e.g., circular RNA, modified nucleosides, or related modalities) is a plus 
 Familiarity with CRISPR-based or other precision gene editing technologies 
 Experience applying computational tools or AI/ML approaches to mRNA sequence design or optimization is a plus 
 Experience translating RNA-based therapeutic technologies from in vitro systems into in vivo animal models, using non-viral (e.g., LNP) or viral (e.g., AAV) delivery systems 
 Working knowledge of human biology and animal models of disease as they relate to therapeutic development 
 Excellent scientific communication skills, with the ability to present complex findings clearly to diverse audiences and contribute to written scientific outputs; strong publication and presentation record, with engagement in the broader scientific community (e.g., conferences, scientific societies) 
 Experience providing day-to-day scientific direction to research associates, interns, or co-op students, and comfort collaborating with and directing the work of external CROs; success operating within a lean, matrixed team, including dotted-line working relationships, is a plus 
 
  This position in the Platform Technology & Innovation team is a rare opportunity to join a small, world-class team doing foundational science with direct and rapid translation to impact patients — for a scientist who brings both rigor and imagination to the hardest problems in RNA engineering.  
       The pay range reflects the full-time base salary range we expect to pay for this role at the time of posting. Base pay will be determined based on several factors including, but not limited to, relevant experience, skills, and education. This role is eligible for an annual short-term incentive award (e.g., bonus) and an annual long-term incentive award (e.g., equity). 
 Prime Medicine offers a comprehensive Total Rewards package with robust health, financial, and wellness benefits—including medical, dental, vision, life insurance, a 401(k) match, and equity programs—along with generous paid time off, wellness days, and company-wide recharge breaks. 
 Our commitment to employee well-being reflects our belief that when we care for our people, we strengthen our ability to put patients first and make meaningful impact together.   U.S. Pay Range   $145,000  —  $161,000 USD      Prime Medicine is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, veteran status, or any other classification protected by law.

Product Designer, Knowledge Graph Intelligence 
  A Career with Point72’s Compliance Team  
 The Point72 Compliance department is an industry-leading team of compliance professionals who support global investment and trading activities by establishing and enforcing the firm’s compliance policies, providing real-time advice, and conducting pre- and post-trade surveillance. Our team is essential to Point72’s success and we provide mentorship, a growth path, and the opportunity for a long-term career with us. 
  What you’ll do  
 As a Product Designer, you will join our Knowledge Graph Intelligence team, which focuses on developing technical applications for investment operations. Specifically, you will: 
 
 Execute the design process for new features and improvements, from concept to delivery, for our suite of investment applications. 
 Collaborate closely with product managers, engineers, and stakeholders to understand requirements and translate them into user-centered design solutions. 
 Conduct user research and usability testing to gather insights and validate design decisions. 
 Create wireframes, prototypes, and high-fidelity designs that adhere to and contribute to our design system. 
 Advocate for UX best practices while fostering a culture of design thinking and customer-centricity across the team. 
 Measure and analyze user engagement to identify opportunities for product improvement. 
 Stay abreast of UX trends, tools, and technologies, and share knowledge with the team to foster innovation. 
 
  What’s required  
 
 5 years of experience in UX design, with a proven track record of delivering user-centric solutions in an agile development environment. 
 A degree in UX design, human-computer interaction, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. 
 A strong portfolio showcasing expertise in UX design, particularly in the context of web applications for financial services or similar complex domains. 
 Demonstrated proficiency in design and prototyping tools, such as Figma and/or Adobe XD, and a solid understanding of HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. 
 Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to articulate design decisions and incorporate feedback from multiple stakeholders. 
 Passion for understanding the needs of users with experience conducting user research and usability testing. 
 Commitment to the highest ethical standards. 
 
  We take care of our people  
 We invest in our people, their careers, their health, and their well-being. When you work here, we provide: 
 
 Fully-paid health care benefits 
 Generous parental and family leave policies 
  Volunteer opportunities  
  Support for employee-led affinity groups representing women, people of color and the LGBT+ community  
 Mental and physical wellness programs 
 Tuition assistance 
 A 401(k) savings program with an employer match and more 
 
  About Point72  
 Point72 is a leading global alternative investment firm led by Steven A. Cohen. Building on more than 30 years of investing experience, Point72 seeks to deliver superior returns for its investors through fundamental and systematic investing strategies across asset classes and geographies. We aim to attract and retain the industry’s brightest talent by cultivating an investor-led culture and committing to our people’s long-term growth. For more information, visit  https://point72.com/ . 
 The annual base salary range for this role is $120,000-$250,000 (USD) , which does not include discretionary bonus compensation or our comprehensive benefits package. Actual compensation offered to the successful candidate may vary from posted hiring range based upon geographic location, work experience, education, and/or skill level, among other things.

At Roofr, we’re obsessed with our customers. We constantly gather feedback to shape, prioritize, and launch the products they truly need. That’s what makes Roofr’s CRM special. We started by building essential sales tools like aerial roof measurements and digital sales proposals. But when our customers asked for a simple, affordable way to manage and scale their entire businesses, we listened. So, we created a CRM that connects these solutions—along with payments, material ordering, and more—into a seamless, powerful platform. With a clear roadmap ahead, we’re excited to continue expanding and leading the market with innovative products. 
 We have an amazing culture, strong financials, and best-in-class company metrics. It’s an exciting time to be part of an extraordinary startup that is already successful, yet still early enough to offer its team significant growth, equity, and the opportunity to make a real impact. 
 This position is for an existing vacancy.   As a  Senior Product Designer  on our design team, you will be part of the  Proposals  product squad. You will play a critical role in shaping the user experience of the tools contractors use to win the job, often balancing competing goals of fidelity, release velocity, delight, and developer bandwidth.  
 You will work closely with product managers, engineers, and other stakeholders to create intuitive, user-centered designs that exceed customer expectations and drive business success. Our goal is to enable you to do the best design work of your career by providing agency as a designer to make critical product decisions.   What you get to do:  
 
 Own the end-to-end design process for the Proposals Squad while collaborating closely with product managers and engineers 
 Work in an iterative design process: initiating UX research, prototyping, usability testing, incorporating internal+external feedback, and evaluating metrics when available 
 Apply strategic thinking to product features, ensuring your design solutions align with company goals 
 Contribute to the design team’s culture through design jams, critiques, retrospectives, and cross-squad initiatives 
 Collaborate with cross-functional teams to gather insights to incorporate into your design solutions 
 Advocate for our users. We are customer-obsessed, and every decision is made with our customers in mind  
 Join a highly-skilled team of product designers that truly look out for one another, support each other, and help each other grow their design skillset  
 
  What you bring to the role:     
 
 4+ years of experience in supporting full product life cycles 
 Ability to break down complex problems to create intuitive, delightful solutions 
 Experience with user research methodologies and demonstrated ability to translate findings into actionable design insights 
 Strong visual design skills with a keen eye for detail 
 Excellent communication and presentation skills, with the ability to articulate design concepts and advocate for your perspective 
 Ability to collaborate across product, engineering, and customer-facing teams to align on goals and execution 
 Comfortable integrating AI tools into your design process, from ideation and prototyping to research synthesis, to move faster without sacrificing craft 
 Growth mindset. You continually seek opportunities to improve processes, tools, and techniques 
 
  Bonus Points:      
 
 Experience designing for construction tech or related software 
 History of designing in fast-paced startup environments 
 Experience utilizing and contributing to design systems 
 You’re not afraid to take risks and lead by vocalizing support for innovative solutions that may not always be immediately obvious to stakeholders 
 
   
 
  Compensation Band: $130,000.00 - $150,000.00 CAD

While many hires fall within the beginning to midpoint of the band to allow for growth over time, we tailor offers based on each candidate’s experience, seniority, and demonstrated impact.

About Tailscale   
 Tailscale is making safe connection effortless by delivering software that makes it easy to securely interconnect people and their devices, no matter where they are. From hobbyists to multinational corporations, teams of every size use Tailscale each day to protect their networks, share access to internal tools, and more. We're building a future for the Internet that's easy, sensible, and safe, like it used to be. Founded in 2019 and fully distributed, we're backed by Accel, CRV, Insight, Heavybit, and Uncork Capital.    About the Role  
 This is a dedicated growth research role. You'll run studies — usability testing, survey research, experimental studies — and collaborate on findings with the Product Growth team. The role is specifically focused on growth-related product surfaces, onboarding flows, acquisition and activation funnels, and the questions that emerge from the growth team's experiment pipeline. It is not focused on generative research for new product development; you will be helping tune and refine delivery of value, though you will partner with other researchers to identify and address fundamental product issues that limit product-led growth. 
 You'll report to the design manager and work most closely with the Growth PM and Growth Designers on a day-to-day basis. The staff UX researcher will be your primary resource for methods and bigger-picture research context. The role is designed to grow from running studies from the team's pipeline and building domain expertise, towards owning the research agenda for growth-related areas with increasing independence. 
  Key Responsibilities  
 Research 
  Run growth research studies.  Your core responsibility is conducting research that supports the growth team's experiment pipeline and tactical questions. 
 
 Own the full study lifecycle for growth research: scoping, recruiting, conducting, analyzing, and communicating results. 
 Design studies and instruments to conduct evaluation and diagnostic discovery for adoption experiences. This includes: 
 
 Behavioural research: moderated and unmoderated usability tests for both formative and evaluative goals. You should be comfortable with experimental methods and able to navigate quantitative statistics for user research.  
 Interviews, mixed methods, and longitudinal studies (eg diary studies) with users and representative populations. 
 Standalone surveys and feedback forms (triggered at different parts of the adoption lifecycle) 
 
 Analyse behavioural data available from logs and use that to inform research thinking, validate hypotheses, and triangulate with experimental/unmoderated test data. 
 Look through other data (community forums, feedback forms, etc.) to proactively identify research opportunities 
 Identify user needs during trial, proof of concept, and adoption phases 
 Model and map adoption behaviours, and define personas accordingly 
 Over time, work towards surfacing research opportunities independently and managing a research program for the growth team. 
 
  Partner with the growth team.  You'll work directly with the Growth PM and Growth Designers to translate hypotheses into study designs and bring findings back in actionable formats. 
 
 Help the growth team test and validate designs. 
 Identify frictions and problems with product adoption. 
 Based on research insights, suggest experiment and design ideas. 
 Work in tandem with the growth team's experiment and A/B testing cadence.  
 Communicate often and quickly about ongoing work, and involve them deeply in the research process as appropriate 
 
 Domain expertise
